scenario: A person plans to keep a phone for about five years and wants one case that still looks acceptable and protects the phone in year four. Previous clear cases yellowed, a leather case failed at the corners, and a soft-touch case became gummy. The frozen material contains one current clear PC-and-TPU case listing, material-mechanism pages, and community observations ranging from more than one year to about three years plus imprecise reports of use for years. It contains no controlled four-year comparison and no exact case model observed for four years with both appearance and protection outcomes.

rules.seller_claim_snapshot_v1: The frozen CASEKOO page is an in-stock 25.99 dollar listing for an iPhone 13 Pro Max case. It describes a rigid polycarbonate back and TPU bumpers, an anti-yellow coating said to resist 99.9 percent of yellowing caused by ultraviolet light and sweat, military-level drop protection, and free replacement within one year. These are seller statements on one current page, not an observed four-year lifetime, an independent aging test, or a controlled drop comparison. The one-year replacement period is shorter than the requested year-four decision horizon.
rules.material_mechanism_boundaries_v1: The polycarbonate source says the material is susceptible to ultraviolet degradation and yellowing, standard resins are unsuitable for long-term ultraviolet exposure, and stabilizers or surface layers can improve weathering resistance. The TPU source distinguishes polyester- and polyether-based TPU, including different hydrolysis resistance, and says aliphatic TPU is used when stable light color and non-yellowing performance are required. The plastic-conservation source lists polyurethane as capable of becoming yellowed, brittle, sticky, and crumbly and says urethane-containing condensation plastics are subject to hydrolysis. The leather source describes heat, moisture, light, handling, and finishes as deterioration factors and notes that temperature fluctuation can produce surface cracks. These mechanisms explain why formulation, additives, coatings, environment, geometry, and use matter. They do not establish how long any named phone case will last or prove that a PC, TPU, polyurethane, or leather label alone predicts year-four condition.
rules.community_duration_and_outcome_scope_v1: The community material contains distinct, non-combinable observations. One author reports an unnamed clear case remaining clear after two years, without a model, material, exposure history, or drop outcome. In another thread, a participant says Apple Leather Cases last about two years before that participant degrades the corners, and a different participant reports an OtterBox Symmetry breaking at the thin silicone strip near the charging port after about three years. A BuyItForLife thread contains a brand-level Spigen report across about four years as a Pixel user with many drops and no cracked screen, a separate imprecise report of a Spigen used for years on a Samsung without problems, and an OtterBox report of a torn port cover, separating rubber shell, difficult warranty use, and one cracked plastic part. A Casetify owner reports more than one year, multiple drops, an undinged case, and bright unscratched graphics, but does not identify an exact model. These are scoped owner observations under uncontrolled use. They may show possible outcomes and failure modes, but they cannot be pooled into one four-year test or transferred across models, materials, phones, environments, and users.
rules.four_year_claim_audit_v1: A defensible audit must keep appearance and protection separate. The strongest named appearance-plus-drop report lasts only more than one year and is not an exact model. The leather and OtterBox reports reach about two and about three years but describe failures rather than intact year-four condition. The unnamed clear case reaches two years for clarity only. The Spigen reports use an unspecified model and either an ambiguous continuity period or an imprecise duration. No frozen source observes one exact case model for four years while recording both acceptable appearance and protection. Therefore the seller's never-yellow and drop-protection language, the material mechanisms, and the owner reports do not justify naming a proven year-four winner.
rules.conditional_purchase_and_monitoring_v1: If a purchase must be made from the frozen material, treat the CASEKOO listing only as a conditional, testable candidate because it exposes a PC-and-TPU architecture, an anti-yellow-coating claim, a drop-protection claim, and a one-year replacement promise. Before buying, verify exact phone fit, exact model and revision, written warranty terms, and whether the resin, coating, and test details are documented; otherwise do not infer them from generic PC or TPU labels. Photograph the unused case against the same neutral background and lighting, record mass and fit at the corners and ports, then repeat photographs and fit checks at regular intervals such as every three months. Log each meaningful drop with height, surface, impact area, visible case damage, and phone outcome. Check for color shift, surface tackiness, coating wear, cracks, looseness, corner or bumper separation, port-strip tearing, and reduced lip coverage. Replace the case when cracks, looseness, separation, persistent tackiness, or reduced retention compromises fit, regardless of appearance. This protocol can create future evidence but cannot retroactively prove a four-year lifetime.
rules.evidence_bounded_case_decision_v1: The admissible answer must distinguish seller claims, material mechanisms, and owner observations; label every observed duration and model limitation; explain the clear-case, leather-corner, soft-touch, and protection branches without transferring evidence across them; and explicitly say that the frozen material cannot identify a case proven to look acceptable and protect in year four. It may name the listed clear case only as a conditional monitored trial, not as a four-year recommendation, and must provide the long-term record and replacement triggers.
